body:
## Summary

In agent mode, Formal AI's intent routing matches text anywhere in the incoming
request — including the *caller's* framing — and treats a declarative sentence as
though it were the user's question. The Gemini CLI prefixes every turn with a
`<session_context>` block containing

```
Today's date is Sunday, August 2, 2026 (formatted according to the user's locale).
```

Formal AI answers **that sentence**: it calls `run_shell_command("date")`, reports the
date, and never acts on the request that follows. Because the CLI injects the line
unconditionally, **every** `gemini` run through Formal AI in agent mode is hijacked —
`gemini` is effectively unusable as a Formal AI client on 0.317.0.

## Reproduction

Script: [`repro-intent-hijack.sh`](https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/blob/main/experiments/issue-2130/repro-intent-hijack.sh) ·
stored output: [`formal-ai-0.317.0-intent-hijack.log`](https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/blob/main/docs/case-studies/issue-2130/data/probes/formal-ai-0.317.0-intent-hijack.log)

Server: `formal-ai serve --agent-mode --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8138` (0.317.0).
Every request below is the same request — `Write a hello world program in Python.` —
over the same protocol with the same two tool declarations. The **only** variable is
one line of caller context.

```
== the session_context the gemini CLI really sends
  <session_context> … Today's date is Sunday, August 2, 2026 …   -> run_shell_command({"command":"date"})

== the same context with only the date sentence removed
  <session_context> … My operating system is: linux …            -> write_file({"content":"print(\"Hello, world!\")","file_path":"main.py"})

== narrowing the trigger to a phrase
  Today's date is Sunday, August 2, 2026.                        -> run_shell_command({"command":"date"})
  The current time is 20:00.                                     -> run_shell_command({"command":"date"})
  The date is Sunday.                                            -> write_file(… main.py)
  Today is Sunday, August 2, 2026.                               -> write_file(… main.py)
  date                                                           -> write_file(… main.py)
  My operating system is: linux                                  -> write_file(… main.py)
  (no context at all)                                            -> write_file(… main.py)
```

Deleting one sentence restores correct behaviour. Nothing else changes.

### End to end through the real CLI

[`e2e-gemini.log`](https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/blob/main/docs/case-studies/issue-2130/data/runs/e2e-gemini.log),
gemini-cli against `formal-ai serve --agent-mode`, prompt `Write a hello world program in Python.`:

```json
{"type":"tool_use","tool_name":"run_shell_command","parameters":{"command":"date"}}
{"type":"tool_result","status":"success","output":"Sun Aug  2 20:20:17 UTC 2026"}
{"type":"message","role":"assistant","content":"The `date` command completed. Output:\n\n```text\nSun Aug  2 20:20:17 UTC 2026\n```"}
{"type":"result","status":"success", …}
```

Exit code 0, `status: "success"`, no `main.py`, and the request was never attempted.
Reproduced identically on three separate runs.

## What is *not* the cause

Each of these was tested against the same server and ruled out — worth recording so
the search space is smaller:

| Hypothesis | Test | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| The Gemini protocol adapter is broken | same request over `/api/gemini` vs `/api/openai/v1` vs `/api/anthropic` | all three correct |
| A session preamble suppresses routing | preamble vs no preamble, no tools declared | both correct |
| Large caller system prompts crowd out the request | system prompt swept 0 → 73,438 prompt tokens | correct at every size |
| Declaring tools breaks routing | same request with/without a `tools` block | both correct |
| Multi-part user turns lose the later parts | `parts:[context, request]` vs one concatenated part | identical — both hijacked |

The trigger is the *phrase*, not the transport, the size, or the message shape.
`Today's date is …` and `The current time is …` fire it; `The date is …`, `Today is …`,
and a bare `date` do not. That pattern points at an intent matcher keyed on
question-like phrasings that is being run over the concatenated prompt without
distinguishing which turn — or which speaker — the text came from.

## Suggested fix

1. **Scope intent matching to the user's actual request.** Route on the final user
   turn only, not on system instructions or context blocks the client injects. Every
   agentic CLI prepends environment framing; treating it as user intent will keep
   producing this class of failure with other phrases (`My operating system is: linux`
   is one `uname` pattern away from the same bug).
2. **Require interrogative or imperative form.** `Today's date is X.` is a statement
   supplying a fact; a matcher that fires on it will also fire on `The current time is
   20:00.`, which it does. Matching `what is the date` / `what time is it` and not
   declarative `X is Y` would fix both observed cases.
3. **When a built-in intent matches but the turn also carries a task, prefer the
   task.** The request `Write a hello world program in Python.` was present, unambiguous,
   and discarded.

## Workaround

None from the client side: the `<session_context>` block is generated by gemini-cli
and cannot be suppressed. Callers can only avoid `gemini` until this is fixed. Hive
Mind currently documents `gemini` + `--model formal-ai` as blocked on this issue.

## Context

Found while diagnosing link-assistant/hive-mind#2130. Related: #904 (the caller's
system prompt leaking into the plan's `goal` field — same root pattern of treating
caller framing as user content) and #906 (naive keyword extraction in request parsing).

Environment: formal-ai 0.317.0, gemini-cli, Linux 6.8.0, Node 24.18.1.
title: Agent mode: caller framing hijacks intent routing — "Today's date is …" makes every gemini run answer with `date`
